public_rationale: The evidence is consistent with continued satisfaction so far: favorable sentiment remained a majority in 2025 and 2026. The earlier decline qualifies that picture. Neither survey establishes a decisive reversal, and neither settles an open-ended promise of continued happiness. The proposed explanation about programmers' training also remains untested here.
limitations: Survey respondents are not necessarily representative of all programmers.
Workplace AI sentiment is broader than satisfaction with autocomplete assistance.
Repeated cross-sectional surveys are not a panel of the same users.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Marcus thinks coders will remain happy with generative AI assistance, because its autocomplete nature is fabulous for their work and they have the training to detect and fix its not-infrequent errors.

statement.excerpt: I think coders will remain happy with generative AI assistance; its autocomplete nature is fabulous for their line of work, and they have the training to detect and fix the not-infrequent errors.
statement.document_title: What if Generative AI turned out to be a Dud?

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that programmers generally continue to find AI assistance satisfactory, not that every programmer is happy.
Favorable attitudes among users are a reasonable indicator of happiness. Adoption alone is insufficient.
The comments about autocomplete and error correction explain the forecast; they do not establish a separately specified causal test.
'I think' expresses confidence rather than an antecedent. No deadline is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Repeated, reasonably representative measurements show sustained satisfaction among programmers using generative-AI assistance. Such evidence supports the observed trajectory but does not alone close an unlimited forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative longitudinal evidence establishes a sustained broad reversal to dissatisfaction among established users, rather than isolated frustration or reduced trust in particular outputs.

evidence.explanation: A majority of respondents expressed favorable attitudes, consistent with continued satisfaction so far. This is a survey snapshot about workplace AI generally, not a longitudinal measure confined to 2023 coding-assistant users.

evidence.excerpt: positive favorability in AI decrease from 72% to 60% year over year.
evidence.locator: Cracks in the foundation are showing as more developers use AI
evidence.explanation: Declining favorability is material caution against an uncomplicated satisfaction story. A remaining favorable majority does not establish broad dissatisfaction or meet the early-resolution rule.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A decisive sustained reversal meeting the early-resolution rule could contradict the forecast. Supporting a bounded version would require a specified horizon and comparable satisfaction measurements over that period.
